clue.text: Each mum coming through carries beach things

indicators.note: the short pieces pass right through the middle of the longer word, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a shop that carries a line stocks and sells it
EA is the standard abbreviation for each
mum as in keep mum: be quiet, hence the hushing sound

explanation.surface: A mother walks in carrying bags full of things for a day at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not a mother but the instruction to stay silent; SEASHELLS is S(EA SH)ELLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shells collected on the sand are typical objects found along the coast, so they are loosely things of the beach.

clue.text: Massage inside vehicle upset residential community

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the combined letters are read from bottom to top
inside places the word for massage within the word for the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a public road vehicle
to massage is to rub

explanation.surface: Someone gets a massage in a van that then overturns, disturbing a quiet neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A suburb is an outlying district of a city where people mainly live rather than work.

clue.text: Unsurpassed stall out of street elevated produce

indicators.note: out of here means without, so the letters for street are taken away from the stall

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the usual abbreviation for street

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means lifted up, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to emit is to give off or produce

explanation.surface: A market stall off the high street sells the best vegetables ever, raised up on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like a noun for fruit and vegetables, but it is the verb emit.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record or high is the best ever achieved, never beaten by anything before.

clue.text: Football move tackles slam dancer at metal show

indicators.note: a footballer who tackles wraps around an opponent, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a header is striking the ball with the head
to slam a door is to bang it

explanation.surface: A football play crashes into a slam-dancing fan at a heavy metal concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Football move' is a header, the ball struck with the head, which is fitting for a fan who shakes their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy metal fans thrash their heads violently in time with the music, and are named for this motion.

clue.text: Playing roles one hasn't won

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so the letters are moved around freely

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor playing parts but never winning an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who finishes without victory in a contest is the defeated party, the person beaten.

clue.text: Forgoing dates, what with theatre job

definitions.note: the answer is the person who does this job

parts.note: to go stag is to attend a party without a partner
eh? is a way of saying what? when you have not heard
and adds one thing to another, like with

explanation.surface: Someone gave up dating, what with their demanding theatre work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dates' are romantic partners, not fruit or days; going stag means without one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand works backstage moving scenery and props, so the term names a person employed in that role at a playhouse.

clue.text: Mostly noodles behind fine physique

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped
behind means placed after, so the shortened noodle word follows the letter for fine

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
ramen are Japanese wheat noodles

explanation.surface: Eating too many noodles shows up behind an otherwise fine body.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's frame is their bodily build, the skeleton and shape that make up their physical form.

clue.text: Frustrate comedic partner, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to thwart a plan
second meaning: a character who sets off another by contrast, such as a straight man

explanation.surface: Annoying the other half of a comedy double act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' warns that a comedy straight man is only one example of the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to thwart; as a noun it is someone whose contrasting qualities set off another performer.

clue.text: Current information supports insect component of vaccine

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so these letters come after

parts.note: an ant is an insect
I is the physics symbol for electric current
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Up-to-date data backs up an insect ingredient in a new vaccine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning up to date, but it is the symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaccine contains a substance that provokes the immune system into making antibodies, which is what this term names.

clue.text: Scramble eggs not eaten for starters, incorporating fish

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so the fish goes inside the selected letters
starters are the opening letters of each of the three words

parts.note: the opening letter of each word
cod is a common fish

explanation.surface: Scrambled eggs left uneaten at breakfast, with some fish mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scramble' is not about eggs here but means to put a message into code.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble a message is to encrypt it so it cannot be read without a key.

clue.text: Tree research site backed by South Africa

indicators.note: backed here means going backwards, so the word for research site runs right to left

parts.note: a lab is a laboratory
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa

explanation.surface: A tree research station funded by South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a tropical American tree whose very light wood is used for models and rafts.

clue.text: Fact is, Tesla breaks still

indicators.note: the letters break into the word for still, splitting it apart and sitting inside

parts.note: static means motionless
taken as written
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: Claim: a Tesla car's brakes still work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' puns on a car's brakes, and Tesla is the SI unit with symbol T, not the car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistic is a single numerical data point, a figure stated as a fact.

clue.text: Emus tangling with birder given payback

indicators.note: things tangling become knotted up and muddled, so the letters are jumbled together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher gets into a scrap with some emus and is compensated afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reimbursed has had money they spent paid back to them, which is a refund or repayment.

clue.text: My retired era, beginning in Disneyland

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word for era is read backwards

parts.note: an age is an era

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of the theme park's name

explanation.surface: A pensioner recalls the era when they first went to Disneyland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned exclamations of surprise, the second a mild oath, so 'My!' and this one are interchangeable.

clue.text: Person exploring a release covered by German artist

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something covered by another is wrapped inside it, so the release sits within the artist

parts.note: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and engraver
to vent is to let out or release

explanation.surface: An explorer's journey is depicted in a work by a German painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exploring unknown lands is a traveller seeking excitement and discovery, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Dictator's hurt nation's capital

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates words to be written down, so it is how the word is spoken

parts.note: a burn is an injury that hurts

explanation.surface: A tyrant has wounded the country's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' is not a tyrant but someone dictating aloud to a typist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bern is the seat of government and de facto capital city of Switzerland.

clue.text: Searing seafood preparation overwhelms daughter

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf completely, so the larger word swallows the letter

parts.note: fish are prepared by scaling them, scraping off the scales
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Cooking fish on a scorching grill proves too much for a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Searing and scalding both describe something extremely hot, enough to burn the skin.

clue.text: Delay evident in reactions to new allegations

indicators.note: evident in means plainly visible within the following words, which carry the letters

parts.note: spans the end of reactions, two whole words and the start of allegations

explanation.surface: Stalling is apparent in how a politician responds to fresh accusations.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last S of reactionS and ends after ALL of allegations.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to obstruct or hold things up by refusing to answer or cooperate, so it means to delay.

clue.text: Using sound oars, used to hard timber

indicators.note: sound means spoken, so both pieces are words heard, not written

parts.note: someone using oars rows a boat; 'sound' in the middle marks the spoken form
would expresses past habit, as in 'he would walk daily'

explanation.surface: A rower with good oars is accustomed to hardwood boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' seems to mean the oars are in good condition, but it signals pronunciation; it sits between 'Using' and 'oars'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewood is a dense, dark tropical hardwood prized for furniture and musical instruments.

clue.text: Old doctor nearly surrounded by paperwork?

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
to doctor results is to rig or falsify them
amid means in the middle of, surrounded by

explanation.surface: An elderly physician almost buried under administrative forms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the verb meaning to tamper with, and 'surrounded by' is a word to be shortened, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding sheets into shapes, so it is literally work done with paper; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Long periods of fame on Strictly

indicators.note: of here means taken from, so the letters come out of the run of words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of fame, the word on and the start of Strictly

explanation.surface: A celebrity enjoys lasting fame after appearing on a TV dance contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly is Strictly Come Dancing, a BBC celebrity ballroom show.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are vast spans of time, used loosely for any very long while.

clue.text: Nervous swallows primarily twitter on the fence

indicators.note: something that swallows takes another thing inside it

parts.note: neural means relating to the nerves

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of twitter

explanation.surface: An anxious bird gulps down its song while perched on a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervous' means of the nerves, not anxious; 'swallows' looks like birds to match twitter and fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the fence is an idiom for refusing to take a side, which is staying impartial.

clue.text: Setback which denied both sides trophy

indicators.note: denied both sides means stripped of its two ends, losing the first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: A team loses on both flanks and is refused the trophy, a real blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is a minor difficulty or temporary problem that interrupts progress.

clue.text: Completely sacred to anyone listening

indicators.note: to someone listening, only the spoken form matters, not the spelling

parts.note: holy means sacred

explanation.surface: Something is utterly sacred to anyone who hears it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholly means entirely or fully, in every respect, the same as completely.

clue.text: Goddess regularly overlooked in ruins

indicators.note: every other letter is skipped at even intervals, so only the alternate ones remain

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An ancient goddess's temple, now in ruins, is regularly ignored by tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow and messenger of the gods.

clue.text: Box in church holds rubbish EU bible set

indicators.note: something that holds another keeps it within, so the next pieces go inside

parts.note: to pen is to confine or box in
CH is the abbreviation for church
tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless junk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A collection box in a church contains worthless European Union bibles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a noun for a container, but 'Box in' is a verb meaning confine; the church piece follows it and the rest goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentateuch is the first five books of the Old Testament, a group of scriptures treated as a unit.

clue.text: Pay for extravagance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cover someone else's bill
second meaning: an indulgence or special luxury

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like paying for one's lavish spending; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to buy something for another person; as a noun, a pleasurable indulgence.

clue.text: Mog raised drink over last of clues

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of clues

explanation.surface: The setter Mog raises a glass after finishing the final clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Mog is this puzzle's setter; mog is also British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mog and puss are both informal British names for a domestic cat.

clue.text: Thicken catalogue with new layout

indicators.note: giving something a new layout rearranges its parts into a different order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A mail-order catalogue gets bulkier after its redesign.
explanation.definitionFit: To coagulate is for a liquid such as blood to set into a semi-solid mass, so to become thicker.

clue.text: Country flower pinned on Romeo

indicators.note: pinned on means attached after, so the river follows the letter for Romeo

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ural flows through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A country bloom pinned onto Romeo's lapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as flow-er, a river, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Country used as an adjective, as in country life, means of the countryside, rural.

clue.text: Mates strain into pubs on vacation

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the strain is placed within the remaining letters
vacation means emptying out, so the inside is cleared, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of pubs
a strain is a tune or melody, as is an air

explanation.surface: Friends belt out a song in bars while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' is music, not effort, and 'on vacation' empties the word rather than meaning a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Mates are partners that come in twos, such as animals breeding together, so they form couples.

clue.text: Tardily gathering how puzzle solvers think

parts.note: late as an adverb, as in arriving late
a rally is a mass gathering

explanation.surface: Crossword solvers who are slow to arrive at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' looks like a container signal but is the noun rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking means approaching problems indirectly and creatively, exactly what cryptic crosswords demand.
